aeronautics_utility_objects.ponder.share: Assemble the structures, then connect their heads with a pneumatic rod.
The rod extends and retracts along the line between the heads.
Return Force pushes or pulls the link toward its target length.
Stretch Resistance opposes motion along the rod, reducing oscillation.
Right-click the rod body to open its settings.
Expected Length sets the target distance between the heads.
A heavy load can overpower a weak Return Force. Increase it to hold the target length.
Higher Stretch Resistance slows extension and compression.
Free mode releases the target length so the link can slide.
Supply rotation to the regulator. Redstone selects a target within the configured length range.
Place the regulator behind a head, facing toward it.
Signal strength selects the target length within the configured redstone range.
Faster shaft rotation changes the target length more quickly.
The regulator stops updating its target when stationary or overstressed.
The hinge axis sets the pin direction independently of the head facing.
The connected end can pivot around the pin axis.
The rod controls the distance between heads; the hinge allows rotation.
Connect joint heads with a brass or andesite rod to choose the link type.
Brass forms a short elastic link. It turns red near its extension limit and breaks beyond it.
Andesite supports longer links and resists changes from the length set when connected.
An andesite link can also break when compressed too far from its original length.
Brass has an extension limit. Andesite limits both extension and compression from its original length.
Right-click with an empty hand to assemble the attached blocks into a rotating physics structure.
An external force must turn the structure. The bearing measures its rotation.
The rear shaft supplies that rotation to Create machinery.
Sneak-right-click the bearing to adjust Resistance.
Resistance opposes physical rotation. It does not set a target RPM.
